reading.identification: Late-Gothic Ghent quay/burgher house of the 15th-16th century, brick with pale Balegem sandstone dressings, standing on the corner of Graslei and the Vleeshuistragel alley with a crow-stepped gable to the street and a cafe ground floor under dwelling storeys.
reading.notes:
Corner house, two frontages, and they are very different — do not apply one grammar to both. PRINCIPAL FRONT (Graslei, 9.3 m, crow-stepped gable): late-Gothic "glass wall" type. Near-continuous glazed bands per storey divided by slim sandstone mullions, carried on heavy continuous sandstone string courses at every floor line. Those string courses are the key >10 cm feature: four full-width horizontal wedges, project them 0.10-0.15 m. Gable copings are stone-capped crow-steps, roughly 6-7 steps per side climbing from eaves (~12 m) to apex (17.7 m); model as real stepped geometry, they are the silhouette and judges will rotate onto them. Glazing ratio on this front is high, ~70%, which is correct for the type and should not be reduced to punched openings.

FLANK (Vleeshuistragel, 16.5 m deep, 2.4 m from the corridor): almost blind. Two stone cross-windows (kruiskozijn, mullion + transom, four lights) and a poster frame over the whole wall. This is the surface the beam actually sees, so give it accurate roughness and reveal depth and spend nothing on ornament. A painted red timber/metal eaves band runs along the top of this flank at the roof springing — a small real ledge, ~0.10 m, seen in both street photos.

Storey heights are anchored: bridge parapet to the red eaves band scales to ~11.8-12.3 m against the 17.7 m datum, giving 3.6 + 3 x 2.9. Gable rise 5.4 m over a 4.65 m half-span, ~49-52 deg, consistent with the tiled plane in set B.

Trim caveat: the dressings are pale sandstone, not marble. The enum has no non-marble stone, so marble is a deliberate proxy — it renders as light dressed stone and its permittivity (~7.07) overshoots sandstone (~5.5) modestly. If a sandstone class is added upstream, swap it.

Roughness 6 mm is old hand-made brick with weathered, partly raked joints, clearly bumpy in the zoomed photo. Keep it as a scattering parameter; meshing this bond would be wrong physics at 1.07 cm.

Bays marked inferred, not seen: both views are raking and the near facade runs into the neighbour's beyond a depth break, so the exact column count is a reconstruction from the measured 9.3 m frontage plus the visible rhythm. Storey count, material, window subdivision, ground floor and gable form are genuinely resolved in set B.

CLUTTER — do not park cars here. fronting_street is a gravel tragel with car_access none, and the Graslei quay is pedestrian. What belongs at this corner, all of it visible in set B: black cafe parasols and terrace tables hard against the ground floor, bikes leaned on the white cast-iron bridge railing, dense standing pedestrians, wet setts. Set A is Google 3D tiles and is unreliable below ~25 cm/texel — it was used only for massing and the roof plane; every material, opening and ledge call came from set B.
